sources.name: ExRx (Kilgore/Rippetoe), age 18-39
sources.population: untrained to elite recreational/strength-trained adults (Kilgore/Rippetoe tables); Elite approaches competitive level
sources.notes: 1RM, total bar weight. null = value not visible in any snippet (not interpolated). Snippets were search-engine summaries; sex of tables inferred from table order (men first, 114-320+; women second, 97-199+) and from World Record column (women 148: 470, 165: 499). ExRx also has age-variant pages (DeadliftStandards40LB/50LB/60LB) with lower numbers which were NOT used. One snippet gave a table 132:135/195/250, 148:155/215/275 ... of unclear sex/age; excluded. ExRx Untrained is much lower than SL Beginner at light body weights for women, and ExRx Novice-Elite are well below SL for men (e.g. 181 lb: ExRx Int 315 vs SL Int ~348 at 180).

sources.name: StrengthLog (user training logs)
sources.population: app users' training logs (21,677 users) - regular gym-goers
sources.mapping: StrengthLog uses the same 5 names (Beginner/Novice/Intermediate/Advanced/Elite); per snippet Intermediate = stronger than 50%, Advanced = stronger than 75% (SL uses 80%); other cut-offs not seen
sources.notes: 1RM lb as listed. Women's lb table seen only up to 140 lb body weight. Advanced percentile (75%) differs from SL's 80%, so Advanced/Elite naturally lower.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: none (all 5 female rows identical to app). No male body-weight row surfaced; only SL's ratio summary (1.00/1.50/2.00/2.50/3.25 x BW) and the unweighted male overview 173/246/336/440/552.

Deadlift.summary: SL female rows match the app exactly. Other gym-goer sources are lower than SL from Novice upward: StrengthLog men are ~8-10% lower at Intermediate (318 vs 348 at 180 lb) and ~10-12% lower at Advanced/Elite; ExRx men 181 lb is ~10% lower at Int/Elite, but ExRx/StrengthLog Beginner is below SL's Beginner for men (150-163 vs 201 at 180 lb). Women: StrengthLog at 120 lb ~5% lower at Intermediate, ~10% lower at Elite.

sources.name: Strength Level (newer snapshot)
sources.notes: Search summary says an older version of the same page (852,835 lifts) listed 230/303/390/488/592 at 180 lb, which equals the app's row. FitnessVolt quoted the same 381/478 values (it mirrors this data) so it is not an independent source.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: App matches the older SL snapshot at 180 lb. Newer snapshot shown in search is ~2-3% lower (223/295/381/478/580).

Sumo Deadlift.summary: No independent gym-goer table found (ExRx has no sumo standard). SL's current sumo numbers appear ~2-3% below the app's at 180 lb male; otherwise consistent.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: none (female 180 matches exactly). SL ratios seen: male 0.75/1.0/1.5/2.0/2.75 x BW, female 0.5 .. 2.0 x BW; unweighted overview male 121/185/266/361/466, female 63/99/146/201/262.

Romanian Deadlift.summary: Only Strength Level data found; the one checked row matches the app. FitnessVolt quotes 180 lb male Intermediate ~274 lb and Advanced ~360 lb (vs app 280/364), but FitnessVolt is a competition-ratio model, so it is only a rough corroboration (within ~2%).

sources.name: FitnessVolt (modeled)
sources.population: modeled from competition-lifter percentiles (2.5M+ competition results) via strength ratios - NOT direct gym-goer shrug data
sources.mapping: FitnessVolt Beginner/Novice/Intermediate/Advanced/Elite -> same names; its percentile cut-offs differ (Beginner = bottom 25%, Intermediate = 50th, Elite = top 10%)
sources.notes: Population is competitive lifters and values are modeled, so the brief's rules make this a weak source; recorded only as a cross-check.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: No SL body-weight rows surfaced; SL unweighted male overview 101/181/288/420/570.

Barbell Shrug.summary: No gym-goer source besides SL. FitnessVolt's modeled table is close to the app's (180 lb: 119/194/292/410/542 vs app 121/192/284/394/515), i.e. within ~3% to Int and ~4-5% higher at Adv/Elite.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: none (male 180 matches exactly; per dumbbell). SL female unweighted overview 13/31/59/94/137.

Dumbbell Shrug.summary: Only SL data found; the checked row matches the app. No other gym-goer standards with numeric tables surfaced.

sources.name: Strength Level (newer snapshot)
sources.notes: From a search-result summary of the SL bodyweight table; consistently lower than the app's rows, suggesting a newer data snapshot. Unweighted male overview seen in two versions: 94/137/192/255/325 and 89/133/188/253/323.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: All 4 male rows differ: SL now ~5-8 lb lower at Beginner/Novice (e.g. 150: 78 vs 84, 115 vs 120), ~5-7 lb lower at Intermediate, ~2-5 lb lower at Advanced/Elite.

Bent Over Row.summary: No ExRx/StrengthLog row table found. The current SL bent-over row table appears ~3-8% below the app's values (largest at Beginner), so the app may be slightly generous at low levels.

sources.name: FitnessVolt one-arm bent-over row (modeled)
sources.population: modeled from ratios to a base lift (competition data), not measured
sources.notes: Only Intermediate (0.43 x BW) and Advanced start (~99) at 180 lb seen. Much lower than SL; modeled, not measured.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: 180 matches. 150 differs slightly: SL shows 33/56/84/115/149 vs app 33/54/81/113/149 (+2-3 lb at Nov/Int/Adv). An older SL snapshot showed 31/53/82/117/157 (150) and 42/67/99/138/180 (180).

Dumbbell Row.summary: App matches current SL within ~3 lb. The only other source (FitnessVolt, modeled) is ~20% lower at Intermediate, but it is not a measured gym-goer table.

sources.name: FitnessVolt seated cable row (modeled)
sources.population: modeled from FitnessVolt strength ratios (competition-based), sex not labeled in snippet
sources.notes: Sex not stated; assumed male because values sit next to SL male values (app male 150: 86/123/168/220/276). Another FitnessVolt page gave a cable-rope row 180 lb male Int ~106 and a seated row Int 122 or 196, so FitnessVolt is internally inconsistent.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: No SL body-weight rows surfaced; SL unweighted overviews male 91/133/186/246/313, female 44/70/104/145/190.

Seated Cable Row.summary: No ExRx/StrengthLog table. FitnessVolt's (low-confidence) 150 lb row is within ~3% of the app's male 150 row. Machine-stack weights vary by brand, so any standard is approximate.

sources.name: ExRx (Kilgore/Rippetoe) Clean, age 18-39
sources.notes: ExRx 'Clean' = power-clean-style catch (bar caught at/above 90 deg knee angle). Women's values read in kg (44 kg: 12.5/27.5/32.5/42.5/52.5; 90 kg: 27.5/50/57.5/75/95) and converted x2.2046, body weights 44 kg->97 lb, 90 kg->198 lb. Age-variant pages CleanStandards40LB/50LB/60LB (lower values) were NOT used.

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: none (all 3 male rows match exactly). Unweighted SL male overview seen in two versions: 102/143/193/250/311 and 102/147/202/266/336.

Power Clean.summary: SL rows match the app. ExRx agrees closely at Intermediate (181 lb: 195 vs SL 198) and Elite (310 vs 301) and is ~7% higher at Advanced, but ExRx Untrained/Novice are much lower (85/160 vs SL 117/154 for Beginner; Novice roughly equal). Women's ExRx is far below SL (e.g. 198 lb Int 127 vs SL ~140 at 200).
